newsitem.title: UK: Britain to evacuate volcano islanders this week.
newsitem.headline: Britain to evacuate volcano islanders this week.

text.p: The British government announced plans on Monday for a partial evacuation of the Caribbean island of Montserrat later this week as fears grew of a massive volcanic eruption there.
The decision to ask the 5,000 inhabitants of the British colony whether they wanted to leave came after a meeting of senior British officials.

"Over the past 24 hours the volcano has become much more dangerous," said International Development Minister George Foulkes, adding that a "massive, cataclysmic-intensive eruption" could no longer be ruled out.
"As a result we have agreed to this voluntary partial evacuation of anyone who wants to leave," said Foulkes, who is due to visit the island at the end of this month.

Foulkes' department said the latest scientific analysis suggested the northern third of the island, previously thought safe from the Soufriere Hills volcano, was now more at risk than previously thought.
Most of the inhabitants who have braved the volcano's increasing activity since 400 years of dormancy ended in July 1995, are now crammed into this northern area, straining resources there.
The British government is opening a transit centre on the nearby island of Antigua, which is already playing host to many fleeing Monserratians.

"Evacuation is expected to start later this week. Monserratians are expected to go to other Caribbean islands and the UK, although some may go elsewhere," the International Development department said in a statement.

The evacuation is expected to be by sea because of the difficulty of flying through the ash and smoke of the volcano. British warship HMS Liverpool is anchored offshore from Montserrat to help co-ordinate the evacuation.
A ferry service to neighbouring islands such as Guadeloupe and Antigua is another option for those wishing to leave Montserrat, which is in the Leeward Islands chain.
The volcano, in the south of the island, has been spewing out rock and ash and has destroyed the capital, Plymouth. At the end of June, it was responsible for 19 deaths.

On Saturday, scientific advice prompted the authorities to order the evacuation of the central area of the island, where some people had fled after Plymouth was hit by a series of eruptions two weeks ago.
The island's population is down to less than half the 11,000 there before the volcano became active again.

The volcano has shattered the island's economy, destroying crops and tourism. It is now dependent on aid, and Britain has committed more than 41 million pounds ($66 million) to help the Montserrat government deal with the disaster.
